_note: Course-specific addendum to youtube/zh_subs/glossary_zh.json for the Practicing the Way course. Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans); the shipped track is converted to Traditional afterwards. Eight sessions taught by several speakers, so a term rendered two ways across sessions is the most likely defect -- these bindings exist to prevent that. Where this file and the Heartbeat glossary disagree, this one wins; where it is silent, the Heartbeat glossary applies.
_does_not_apply: The Heartbeat glossary's `church` block is about Heartbeat: Pastor Josh, the campuses, Gold Coast/Brisbane/Melbourne. None of it appears in this course -- do not import those names.
The brief says the sermon is mainly Exodus 3 (the burning bush). That is a different job. This course ranges across the Gospels, with Genesis, the Psalms and the Epistles alongside.
`shepherd` as Heartbeat's lay leadership title (小组长) is irrelevant here. In this course the word is a Scripture metaphor -- follow the CUV wording of the verse being quoted.
_core_terms_note: The apprentice/disciple distinction is the one that matters most. This course deliberately says `apprentice` where most teaching says `disciple`, to recover the sense of learning a trade by working beside a master. Collapsing both to 门徒 erases the whole point, so keep 学徒 for `apprentice` and 门徒 for `disciple`, and never swap them even when they appear in the same sentence. `Practicing the Way` is the course's own name: leave it in Latin script rather than translating it, and keep the spaces -- cjk.wrap() protects Latin words from being broken mid-word.
_people_note: Writers quoted across more than one session. These four -- 陶恕, 魏乐德, 劳伦斯弟兄, 盖恩夫人 -- are the established renderings in Chinese Christian publishing and are safe. A name with no settled Chinese form stays in Latin script: a plausible-looking transliteration a reader has never seen is worse than the English, because they cannot look it up. `Thomas a Kempis` has two competing forms (Protestant 托马斯·肯培 against Catholic 金碧士) and was NOT settled here -- leave it in Latin script or confirm before shipping. Batches are translated in parallel by different agents, so any name not pinned here WILL come back rendered two ways; normalise across sessions before building the tracks.

_ambiguous.practice: As a noun in this course it is almost always one of the nine practices: 操练. As an ordinary verb (`we practice what we love`) translate normally -- 练习 or 实践 -- and do not force 操练.
_ambiguous.formation: 属灵塑造 when it means spiritual formation, which is nearly always. Plain 形成 is wrong here.
_ambiguous.Rule of Life: 生活准则 every time, including when the speaker shortens it to `your Rule` or `a Rule`. Never 规则 -- it is a trellis for growth, not a list of rules, and 规则 inverts the meaning the session spends its length establishing.
_ambiguous.way: Capital-W `the Way` (the early church's name for itself, Acts 9:2) is 这道. Lowercase `a way of life` is ordinary: 生活方式.
